thread.title: Asian markets mostly up, as Apple suppliers get a boost

author: morningstar.com
title: Asian markets mostly up, as Apple suppliers get a boost
text:
By Dow Jones Newswire
Nikkei rises after BOJ statement; stocks in China sink after tariff report
After some initial sluggishness, Asia-Pacific stocks generally improved as Wednesday's trading day progressed. But there were no blowout gains occurring, with nearly all rising indexes up no more than 0.5% and many seeing advances of 0.2% of less.
The overnight bounce in the U.S. helped, along with earnings news both local and overseas, including Apple's (AAPL) strong earnings report.
Japan's Nikkei rose 0.5% a day after the Bank of Japan maintained its ultraloose monetary policy (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bank-of-japan-surprises-by-keeping-its-ultra-easy-monetary-policy-in-place-2018-07-31). Honda (HMC) shares jumped after reporting an 11% increase in first-quarter operating profit, which took most analysts by surprise. The news drove gains across much of the sector, along with a weaker yen. Toyota (7203.TO) , which reports earnings Friday, was up 1%.
South Korea's Kospi rose 0.4% although Apple suppliers such as Samsung (005930.SE) and LG Innotek (011070.SE) gave up some of their early gains. Taiwan's Taiex rose as Apple manufacturer Foxconn (2354.TW) gained more than 1%.
Stocks in China retreated amid a report that President Donald Trump's advisers are urging 25% tariffs on $200 billion of Chinese goods (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/advisers-urge-trump-to-raise-tariffs-to-25-on-200-billion-of-chinese-goods-2018-07-31). The Shanghai Composite slid 0.3% while the smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite fell about as much. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index dipped 0.2%, as Apple supplier Sunny Optical (2382.HK) gave up almost all of its post-Apple-earnings bounce.
Australia's benchmark index overcame early losses to eke into positive territory amid weakness in commodity stocks. Oil Search Limited (OSH.AU) was down 0.4% while mining giant BHP Billiton (BHP.AU) gained about 1%. Stocks in New Zealand fell.
Malaysia's benchmark was down slightly after having risen 16 of the past 17 days, while Singapore's Strait Times Index was up slightly.
-Dow Jones Newswire;
07-31-18 2346ET
